Package frc.robot.subsystems.arm

Class ArmSubsystem

java.lang.Object
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.SubsystemBase
frc.robot.subsystems.arm.AbstractArmSubsystem
frc.robot.subsystems.arm.ArmSubsystem
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.wpi.first.util.sendable.Sendable, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem, Subsystem, AutoCloseable
public class ArmSubsystem extends AbstractArmSubsystem
The arm implementation robot teams instantiate against real hardware.

This class talks to a motor directly. There is no IO layer between it and the mechanism: the position loop, the encoder scaling, and the motor commands all live here, which is where a team integrating this library will actually be working. Simulation is a separate class — SimArmSubsystem — rather than a second IO behind the same subsystem, so a team reading this file sees only the code that runs on their robot.

What this class does

  • Drives a single motor through WPILib's MotorController abstraction, so it works with any PWMSparkMax, PWMTalonFX, PWMSparkFlex, or PWMVictorSPX without change. A team with a vendor library should subclass this and override applyVolts(double) to use the vendor's API, which gives onboard control and better telemetry.
  • Closes the position loop with a WPILib PIDController plus ArmFeedforward.
  • Reads the joint angle from a quadrature Encoder and conditionally from limit switches.

Hardware IDs come from the caller. Everything wired — CAN ID, encoder channels, limit switch channels, inversion — is a constructor argument, so a team configures their robot without editing library source. 


 ArmSubsystem arm = new ArmSubsystem(
     new PWMSparkMax(1),        // motor
     false,                     // inverted
     new Encoder(2, 3),         // quadrature encoder
     new DigitalInput(4),       // lower limit
     new DigitalInput(5),       // upper limit
     ArmHardware.CONSTANTS);    // mechanism description

Gains are a starting point. They come from Constants.HardwareDefaults and are sized so a plausible mechanism moves under control on first run. Every team must tune on their own hardware, because gains depend on gearing, mass, and friction this library cannot know. Call setGains(double, double, double) to retune at runtime.

      public ArmSubsystem(edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.motorcontrol.MotorController motor, boolean inverted, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.Encoder encoder, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.DigitalInput lowerLimit, edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.DigitalInput upperLimit, ArmConstants constants)
      Creates an arm over a WPILib motor controller and sensors.
      Parameters:
      motor - the motor controller that receives commands
      inverted - whether the motor turns opposite its positive direction
      encoder - a quadrature encoder measuring joint angle
      lowerLimit - the lower travel limit switch, or null if the mechanism has none
      upperLimit - the upper travel limit switch, or null if the mechanism has none
      constants - the physical description of the mechanism

      protected edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle sampleAngle()
      Description copied from class: AbstractArmSubsystem
      Returns the arm's current joint angle.

      Implementations supply this from their own sensor — an encoder for hardware, the plant for a simulation. The shared layer calls it rather than caching a value, so a logger or a test always sees the live reading.

    • holdAngle

      protected void holdAngle(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Angle angle)
      Description copied from class: AbstractArmSubsystem
      Drives the arm to hold angle.

      Called once per loop while the mechanism is enabled. Implementations close the loop however suits their hardware: a vendor motor controller's onboard position control, or a WPILib PIDController plus feedforward, as ArmSubsystem and SimArmSubsystem both do.

      angle is already clamped to the travel range, so implementations need not re-validate it.

      Specified by:
      holdAngle in class AbstractArmSubsystem
      Parameters:
      angle - the angle to hold, measured from the zero position

    • driveOpenLoop

      protected void driveOpenLoop(double velocityRotationsPerSecond)
      Description copied from class: AbstractArmSubsystem
      Drives the arm open-loop at a velocity.

      Not reached from any command in this API; it exists so a subclass can build a calibration routine — drive into the lower stop until AbstractArmSubsystem.isAtLowerLimit() trips, then AbstractArmSubsystem.zeroPosition() — without reaching around the abstraction for raw voltage.

      Specified by:
      driveOpenLoop in class AbstractArmSubsystem
      Parameters:
      velocityRotationsPerSecond - the velocity to drive at, positive raising the arm

    • releaseOutput

      protected void releaseOutput()
      Description copied from class: AbstractArmSubsystem
      Stops commanding the mechanism.

      Called while idle and on SubsystemBase.stop(). Whether the arm then holds or sags is the hardware's brake mode, not a decision this method makes.

      Specified by:
      releaseOutput in class AbstractArmSubsystem

    • isReal

      public boolean isReal()
      Description copied from interface: Subsystem
      Returns whether this mechanism is driving real hardware.

      Callers use this to skip hardware-only work, and tests use it to skip assertions that only make sense against real motors. A simulated implementation returns false.

      Returns:
      true for real hardware, false for a simulated implementation
